correctness.rationale: A normalized stationary Green solution with the exact permeability convention yields the closed point-source current. The dimensionless profile factors as z sinh(uz)/sinh(z) times 1/[coth(z)+k/z]. The first factor has strictly negative logarithmic second derivative for 0<u<1; coth(z) and k/z are log-convex, making the reciprocal sum log-concave. Zero endpoint limits give exactly one global optimizer. Explicit mixed derivatives of the log profile give strict source/permeability monotonicity. Uniform large-z asymptotics of the logarithmic derivative with delta z fixed and delta k convergent establish the unique positive limiting root, including delta k to infinity, and the exact 1-to-4 crossover. The packaged checker passes 313 deterministic tests, supplementing the proof; it is not an infinite certification.

originality.rationale: The exact stationary current and qualitative nonmonotone interfacial entropy belong to prior work. Here, an independent strict log-concavity proof establishes a unique reset-frequency maximizer for current at fixed permeability, two strict parameter monotonicities, and the arbitrary-contact-conductance near-interface scaling from one to four. The three closest published mathematical records cover permeability optimization for entropy or forward-current tomography, which neither state nor imply the optimization and singular-contact conclusions without further analysis. Full-text comparison was performed. Unindexed or unrecognized stronger work remains possible.
residual_risks: Some global optimization facts may be derivable quickly from published forward equations, though their statements do not already cover the theorem.
Unindexed or inaccessible equivalent results may predate this analysis; no independence or priority certification.
Care is required when comparing intrinsic versus effective membrane permeability conventions; the present result defines its flux convention explicitly.

value.rationale: The measurable steady membrane throughput, distinct from entropy, has a physically motivated optimization problem. Strict global uniqueness and the direction of parameter shifts are structural transport laws, not an isolated numerical optimum. The source-near-membrane singular perturbation identifies eta=2 kappa ell/D as the natural dimensionless crossover and proves a sharply different universal 1 versus 4 scaled optimum, of potential value in comparing poorly transmitting and highly transmitting barriers. Neither result is a generic consequence of having a nonmonotone current curve; the proof supplies genuinely global and asymptotic analysis.
